extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, federal agencies, technologists, companies, civil society, and the American public
extracted.subtask_description: A U.S. federal policy blueprint laying out core protections and concrete government actions to guide the design, development, procurement, use, and oversight of automated systems (AI) so they protect civil rights, privacy, and public safety. It targets federal agencies, industry, technologists, and the public for implementation and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe and Effective Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: You should be protected from unsafe or ineffective systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated technologies should be designed, developed, and deployed so they do not produce unsafe or ineffective outcomes. The fact sheet emphasizes the need for transparency, accountability, and privacy to avoid systems that replicate or deepen social inequalities; governments and companies should adopt practices to ensure safety and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic Discrimination Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: You should not face discrimination by algorithms and systems should be used and designed in an equitable way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and use of automated systems must prevent embedding or amplifying bias and discrimination. The fact sheet cites harms (surveilling workers, falsely accusing students, denying benefits, wrongful arrests) as examples of algorithmic discrimination and calls for enforcement, guidance, toolkits, and multi-agency action to address these harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: You should be protected from abusive data practices via built-in protections and you should have agency over how data about you is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should include privacy-preserving design and give individuals control over data collection and use. The fact sheet points to federal actions (e.g., FTC exploring rules to curb commercial surveillance and lax data security) and to aligning new practices with existing privacy regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: You should know that an automated system is being used and understand how and why it contributes to outcomes that impact you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals should receive notice when automated decision-making affects them and explanations of how the system contributed to outcomes. The fact sheet highlights CFPB guidance that creditors must provide specific and accurate explanations for adverse credit actions even when relying on 'black-box' models, and agency pilots/requirements (e.g., VA) to inform people when AI is used in healthcare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Options (Opt-out and Human Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: You should be able to opt out, where appropriate, and have access to a person who can quickly consider and remedy problems you encounter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated systems should not be the sole recourse; appropriate opt-outs and timely human review or remediation must be available. Agencies are directed to ensure processes for human consideration and remediation of errors and harms from automated systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Blueprint to Fill Policy Gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Where law or policy does not already provide guidance, the Blueprint should be used to inform policy-making to fill those gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When existing laws or policies are silent or insufficient for AI-related harms, the Blueprint's protections and recommended practices should guide new rules, guidance, and enforcement priorities across government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveillance Reporting Enforcement to Protect Workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ramping up enforcement of required surveillance reporting to protect worker organizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department of Labor will enforce surveillance reporting obligations to limit abusive worker monitoring practices and protect labor organizing. This is a compliance and enforcement standard for employer surveillance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment Algorithm ADA Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment algorithms must comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and related antidiscrimination obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEOC and DOJ issued technical assistance and guidance in May 2022 addressing how employment algorithms intersect with the ADA; employers and vendors should follow this guidance to avoid discriminatory impacts on workers with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability-Inclusive Tools and Playbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt disability inclusion resources (AI & Disability Inclusion Toolkit; Equitable AI Playbook) when deploying AI in employment and other contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and employers are pointed to toolkits and playbooks (e.g., Partnership on Employment & Accessible Technology) as concrete resources to operationalize accessibility and equitable AI practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimagined Hiring and Recruitment Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote equal employment opportunity by reimagining hiring/recruitment practices including the use of automated systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEOC and Department of Labor launched a multi-year collaborative effort to redesign hiring and recruitment so automated tools support—rather than undermine—equal opportunity; this implies design, testing, and oversight criteria for hiring tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTC Rulemaking on Commercial Surveillance, Algorithmic Discrimination, and Data Security
rubrics_metrics.description: FTC is exploring rules to curb commercial surveillance, algorithmic discrimination, and lax data security practices that could violate Section 5 of the FTC Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial actors should expect regulatory rulemaking that may restrict surveillance-based business models, address algorithmic discrimination, and strengthen data security obligations under unfair or deceptive practices authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explainability Requirement for Credit Decisions (CFPB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal anti-discrimination law requires creditors provide consumers with specific and accurate explanations when credit applications are denied or other adverse actions are taken, even if the creditor is relying on a black-box credit model using complex algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creditors must provide actionable explanations for adverse decisions; CFPB is enforcing against algorithmic discrimination in finance and hiring technologists to support oversight. This sets an explainability and fairness standard for financial models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education AI Recommendations: Safety, Fairness, Efficacy, and Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Define specifications and guidelines for the safety, fairness, and efficacy of AI models used within education; provide tools for universal design for learning and align with education data privacy regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department of Education will issue recommendations (by early 2023) to give educators, parents, students tools and guidelines, including guardrails and specifications to protect students and support equitable educational uses of AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit Algorithmic Discrimination in Clinical Decision-Making (HHS Proposed Rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed HHS rule would prohibit discrimination by algorithms used in clinical decision-making by covered health programs and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health care providers and developers subject to covered programs must ensure clinical decision-making algorithms do not discriminate; HHS will also solicit public comment and conduct evidence-based examinations of health care algorithms for racial and ethnic disparities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-Based Examination of Health Care Algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will release an evidence-based examination of health care algorithms and racial and ethnic disparities for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies will evaluate algorithmic impacts in healthcare using evidence and public input to inform policy and rulemaking aimed at reducing disparities caused by AI systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Equity by Design Vision and Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance health equity by releasing a vision for 'Health Equity by Design' that includes methods to reduce algorithmic discrimination in healthcare algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS's vision will outline concrete methods and design principles to prevent bias in healthcare technology and encourage equitable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare Policy to Encourage Bias Prevention by Developers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Medicare rulemaking processes to explore how policy can encourage software developers to prevent and mitigate bias in algorithms and predictive modeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal procurement and payment policy (e.g., Medicare) can create incentives for developers to design less biased, better-validated models for healthcare.

rubrics_metrics.name: VA Principle-Based Ethics Framework and Transparency for Veterans
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute a Principle-Based Ethics Framework for Access to and Use of Veteran Data and pilot programs (AI@VA) to provide veterans with information about any AI system used in their healthcare and ensure AI risks are managed during human subjects research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VA will require ethical governance of veteran data, transparency about AI use in care, and mechanisms to manage risks in research contexts — a model for ethical transparency and oversight in government health systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on Tenant Screening Algorithms (HUD)
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD will release guidance addressing the use of tenant screening algorithms in ways that may violate the Fair Housing Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Landlords, screening companies, and regulators should ensure tenant screening tools do not produce discriminatory outcomes and comply with fair housing laws; guidance will clarify problematic practices and compliance expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination Quality Control Standard for Automated Valuation Models
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies regulating mortgage financing will include a nondiscrimination quality control standard in a proposed rule establishing quality control standards on automated valuation models (AVMs) so these models do not rely upon biased data that could replicate past discrimination in housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory standards for AVMs will require quality control processes to detect and prevent biased inputs or outputs that perpetuate housing discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: USAID AI Action Plan: Embed Risk Mitigation in Programming
rubrics_metrics.description: USAID commits to embedding risk mitigation in AI programming and shaping a global Responsible AI agenda through initiatives like Advancing Digital Democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International programming should integrate risk mitigation and rights-respecting practices into AI projects, influencing global norms and capacity-building in responsible AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement Policies and Guidance to Prevent Algorithmic Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop new policies and guidance for using and buying AI products and services that are based on effective and promising practices to prevent and address bias and algorithmic discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal procurement will adopt standards and best practices so agencies purchase AI that meets fairness, safety, and civil-rights-consistent requirements; vendors must satisfy these procurement criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish Inventories of Government AI Use Cases for Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish inventories of non-classified and non-sensitive government AI use cases to advance transparency and trust in the federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should catalog AI deployments publicly and implement approved plans to ensure AI systems comply with civil rights, civil liberties, and privacy laws and policies; this transparency supports oversight and public accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE Principles and AI Risk Management Playbook
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE will release Principles and Guidelines for Advancing Responsible and Trustworthy AI and an AI Risk Management Playbook suggesting mitigations to proactively manage AI risks such as algorithmic discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical and organizational mitigations recommended by DOE (via playbook) are expected to be practical steps for risk assessment, testing, and governance to reduce discrimination and other AI harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD AI Ethical Principles and Implementation Pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Defense operates under AI Ethical Principles and a Responsible AI Strategy & Implementation Pathway to assist the defense enterprise in upholding these principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defense deployments of AI must adhere to ethical principles and follow an implementation pathway that operationalizes those principles in procurement, development, and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligence Community Principles of AI Ethics and AI Ethics Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Intelligence Community operates under Principles of AI Ethics and an associated AI Ethics Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intelligence use of AI is governed by community-specific ethical principles and frameworks to manage risk and align AI practices with legal and civil-rights obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIST Risk Management Framework and Playbook Companion
rubrics_metrics.description: NIST is developing a risk management framework to help technologists incorporate considerations of fairness, safety, and privacy into the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI products, services, and systems; an online Playbook companion will provide recommended actions to operationalize these considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technologists and organizations should use NIST's RMF and Playbook to operationalize fairness, safety, and privacy throughout the AI lifecycle, using recommended actions for implementation and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Support for Trustworthy AI Research
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Science Foundation supports AI research — including research into the fairness, security, safety, and trustworthiness of AI systems — with over $700 million in investments annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained research funding is a criterion for advancing technical and social-science knowledge to improve AI trustworthiness; researchers and institutions should align proposals with these priority areas.
